problem: Existing automatic prompt optimization approaches cannot effectively handle auto-routing scenarios that require optimizing prompts across diverse models and competing objectives simultaneously.
approach: TAMPO constructs a heterogeneity-aware dataset and trains an uncertainty-aware reward model as an offline proxy, then learns a multi-objective conditional policy for robust prompt generation guided by user preference vectors.
contribution: Achieves stable performance across 86 tasks and diverse models with flexible, cost-effective deployment for auto-routing in LLM-based systems.

problem: Transformer-based decoders treat error-correcting codes as generic sequences, ignoring their algebraic properties and missing opportunities for structured improvement.
approach: Proposes a plug-and-play decoding method that integrates cyclic code structure into Transformer decoders via circulant priors, enabling learnable error correction patterns linked to code properties.
contribution: Achieves average bit error rate reduction by an order of magnitude while reducing parameters by approximately 97% compared to standard Transformer decoders.

problem: Forecasting M&A deal outcomes requires long-context reasoning over hundreds of pages of technical documents, but existing LLM forecasting work lacks such depth and domain specificity.
approach: Combines expert-guided context engineering with finetuning on hindsight-guided reasoning traces from historical deals to output probability distributions over three mutually exclusive outcomes.
contribution: Achieves Brier score of 0.151 on 400+ large deals, 24% below calibrated market-implied probabilities and 25-42% below frontier LMs.

problem: Vision-language models use text as an intermediate proxy for affect analysis, but linguistic templates are discrete and incompatible with continuous valence-arousal regression.
approach: AURA replaces linguistic proxies with a self-organizing archetype manifold grounded in perceptual visual resemblance, adaptively allocating representational density by affective complexity.
contribution: Enables accurate continuous regression and reshapes affective taxonomies via interpretable visual primitives, achieving state-of-the-art on discrete and continuous tasks.

problem: Bridge models exploit clean priors in data-to-data generation but lack principled guidance methods to enhance prior exploitation at inference time.
approach: Proposes training-free Prior Guidance that contrasts weak unseen priors with seen priors via scaling factors, plus frequency-modulated prior guidance tailored to generative dynamics.
contribution: Consistently improves pre-trained bridge models across diverse image translation tasks without retraining, with cascaded framework achieving complementary strengths.

problem: Materials generation requires producing diverse candidates satisfying constraints, but naive preference optimization on coordinate-based representations causes mode collapse.
approach: PLaID++ applies preference optimization with a compact, symmetry-informed Wyckoff text representation that improves efficiency and encourages generalization from physical priors.
contribution: Generates thermodynamically stable, unique, and novel crystal structures at >50% greater rate than prior methods via symmetry-constrained text representation.

problem: Backdoor attacks on fine-tuned LLMs remain mechanistically opaque, making it difficult to understand and eliminate backdoor threats.
approach: Backdoor Attribution uses tripartite causal analysis with a Backdoor Probe to identify learnable backdoor features, then Backdoor Attention Head Attribution pinpoints responsible heads.
contribution: Ablating ~3% of attention heads reduces Attack Success Rate by >90%, and a single vector intervention can boost ASR to ~100% or suppress to ~0%.

problem: Neural retrievers in RAG systems have blind spots: entities relevant to queries but with low embedding similarity are not retrieved.
approach: ARGUS predicts blind-spot risk pre-index via Retrieval Probability Score from entity embedding geometry, then performs targeted document augmentation from knowledge bases.
contribution: Achieves +3.4 nDCG@5 and +4.5 nDCG@10 improvements across retrievers with substantially larger gains on challenging subsets.

problem: Direct adaptation of diffusion models to remote sensing disregards physical laws, causing spectral distortion and radiometric inconsistency.
approach: AnyBand-Diff uses spectral-prior-guided diffusion with Masked Conditional Diffusion, dual stochastic masking, and Physics-Guided Sampling leveraging differentiable physical models.
contribution: Achieves accurate spectral reconstruction and realistic remote sensing image generation with rigorous physical constraints across pixel, region, and global levels.

problem: Choosing the correct embedding dimension for network models is difficult, and little is known about behavior when dimension is misspecified.
approach: Analyzes dimension misspecification under random dot product graphs using random matrix theory, showing oversizing slows convergence while undersizing creates fundamental error floors.
contribution: Establishes theoretical bounds on estimation error under both over- and under-specified dimensions, with synthetic experiments confirming theoretical predictions.

problem: Context management in agentic models incurs substantial decoding overhead from summarization tokens, significantly affecting end-to-end latency.
approach: CoMem decouples memory management from agent workflow via asynchronous k-step-off pipeline that overlaps summarization with inference, with reward-driven training aligning memory model.
contribution: Provides 1.4x latency improvements on SWE-Bench-Verified while preserving performance, with favorable scaling under increased system throughput.

problem: Achieving flexible distortion-perception tradeoff traversal in zero-shot inverse problems remains inefficiently characterized for diffusion-based methods.
approach: MAP-RPS starts with MAP estimation providing low-distortion initialization, then re-noised posterior sampling progressively improves perceptual quality with theoretical guarantees.
contribution: Enables effective D-P tradeoff traversal using a single diffusion model, with latent-space variant LMAP-RPS leveraging pre-trained latent diffusion backbones.

problem: Gated linear attention models for in-context learning have fixed memory capacity prone to interference, especially on long sequences.
approach: Palimpsa uses Bayesian metaplasticity to tie attention plasticity to importance state grounded by priors capturing accumulated knowledge, viewing ICL as continual learning.
contribution: Transforms non-metaplastic models into metaplastic ones, significantly expanding memory capacity and outperforming baselines on MQAR and reasoning tasks.

problem: Large Multimodal Models struggle with region-level perception, especially for multiple regions simultaneously or requiring global context.
approach: CSteer uses training-free representation editing via pre-computed contextual vectors that implicitly represent visual referring behaviors like region differentiation and global attention.
contribution: LMMs with CSteer outperform dedicated referring LMMs in most cases, achieving state-of-the-art without fine-tuning or architectural modifications.

problem: Active view selection for 3D reconstruction typically uses surrogate signals like parameter uncertainty, misaligned with rendering fidelity.
approach: GO-PRE formulates next-best-view selection as maximizing reduction of average marginal predictive entropy over target view manifold, enabling efficient real-time computation.
contribution: Consistently improves active reconstruction performance and provides more reliable uncertainty quantification compared to state-of-the-art.

problem: Multiview subspace clustering suffers from inadequate capture of high-order correlations and sensitivity to noise, with difficulty preserving local geometry.
approach: Proposes nonconvex regularized MvSC with deep priors that characterizes low-rank structure, suppresses outliers, and preserves local patterns via deep networks.
contribution: Develops efficient ADMM-based algorithm with convergence guarantees, demonstrating superiority over existing methods on various datasets.

problem: Truncated positional encodings for GNNs are commonly used in practice but their theoretical properties and expressivity remain unknown.
approach: Establishes theoretical analysis showing truncated spectral and random-walk PEs differ fundamentally in expressive power under truncation.
contribution: Shows truncated spectral PEs are no longer stronger than 1-WL test, with experiments indicating mixed truncated PE families are preferable on real datasets.

problem: Kidney transplant survival prediction is challenging due to complex biomarker-patient interactions and censoring in the data.
approach: FunCQNet integrates deep neural networks with censoring-adjusted sequential quantile loss to approximate interaction-dependent coefficients, plus conformal inference for significance.
contribution: Provides precise multi-quantile predictions on kidney transplant data with clinically significant age-dependent interaction patterns.

problem: Heterogeneous tables have varying headers with shared semantics, making it difficult to induce domain-specialized semantics from local evidence alone.
approach: NAVI uses segment-centric pretraining treating header-value pairs as units for aggregating schema and column-level evidence via Masked Segment Modeling and Entropy-driven Alignment.
contribution: Improves reconstruction, semantic consistency, and downstream utility on heterogeneous in-domain tables across evaluation settings.

problem: Traditional CAPTCHAs are obsolete as advanced reasoning models achieve 90% pass rates on complex logic puzzles, requiring new defense mechanisms.
approach: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs exploit the human-agent cognitive gap via dynamic tasks requiring adaptive intuition rather than granular planning, with scalable data generation.
contribution: Establishes robust defense mechanism for agentic era via large-scale evaluation framework capable of generating effectively unbounded CAPTCHA instances.

problem: Inference-time alignment via reward feedback lacks theoretical foundations, especially for practical settings using neural network reward models.
approach: Assumes true reward lies in Besov spaces capturing non-uniform smoothness, comparing neural networks to linear estimators and analyzing multi-step alternating algorithms.
contribution: Shows feature learning capability of neural networks is crucial for improving performance, with multi-step algorithms improving regret especially under local structure.

problem: Scene text editing typically relies on image background while neglecting target region details, limiting to pre-defined glyphs and degrading to text rendering.
approach: Proposes self-prompting method constructing style and glyph prompts directly from original image without additional encoders, using two-stage training on diffusion transformer.
contribution: Achieves open-vocabulary and style-consistent text editing across various languages with state-of-the-art text accuracy and style consistency.

problem: Vision-prompt-based image editing introduces new attack surface where malicious instructions are conveyed through visual inputs rather than text.
approach: Proposes Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attack that conveys malicious instructions via visual inputs, introduces IESBench safety benchmark, and proposes training-free defense via introspective reasoning.
contribution: Achieves 80.9% attack success on Nano Banana Pro and 70.1% on GPT-Image-1.5, with defense substantially improving safety without auxiliary models.

problem: Any-dimensional models accepting inputs of varying sizes lack clear universality definitions since traditional universality applies only to fixed-size inputs.
approach: Develops systematic approach identifying any-dimensional functions with unique functions in infinite-dimensional limit spaces, using symmetries and input relations.
contribution: Establishes any-dimensional universality framework, shows existing architectures fail universality, and proposes modifications restoring it.

problem: The score matching gap in diffusion models relates KL divergence to score matching loss but remains loose and non-descriptive of actual sample quality.
approach: Provides theoretical analysis developing tighter bounds for KL, reverse KL, and Wasserstein distance by exploiting regularity of score estimators and contraction properties.
contribution: Shows score approximation quality has more impact on closing the gap for low noise scales, using entropy flows and Sobolev inequalities.

problem: Recovering correspondences between embedding clouds from different encoders over partially overlapping datasets is challenging with only vector information.
approach: Vector Linking exploits local geometric consistency in contrastive encoders via iterative geometric embedding hashing using Beta-Bernoulli posteriors.
contribution: Recovers accurate and robust vector links under varying overlap and seed budgets with applications to vector database integration.

problem: Linear probing of vision transformers uses only last-layer representations, overlooking that task-relevant information is distributed across layers.
approach: Attentive Layer Fusion learns to dynamically identify and combine representations from all ViT layers, combining low-level structural cues with high-level semantics.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains over standard linear probes on 20 diverse datasets and multiple pretrained models, with tasks different from pre-training benefiting most.

problem: Existing reward-based text-to-video post-training relies on large-scale annotations or misaligned embeddings, limiting scalability and supervision quality.
approach: PISCES uses Dual Optimal Transport to align reward signals at distributional and token levels, enabling annotation-free quality and semantic rewards.
contribution: Outperforms annotation-based and annotation-free methods on VBench with human preference studies validating effectiveness for short and long-video generation.

problem: Instruction data curation struggles to simultaneously maintain quality, diversity, and distributional consistency without distinguishing semantic redundancy from defects.
approach: Cure-SFT uses coarse-to-fine diagnostic-guided curation removing redundancy via stratified sampling, applying teacher models for triage, and targeted defect remediation.
contribution: Surpasses full-data instruction tuning using only 10% of data budget, consistently outperforming selection and rewriting baselines.

problem: De novo molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectrometry remains limited by poor scalability during both training and inference.
approach: FRIGID introduces diffusion language model generating structures via intermediate fingerprints and chemical formulae, with inference-time scaling via forward fragmentation refinement.
contribution: Achieves 18% Top-1 accuracy on MassSpecGym and triples leading methods on NPLIB1, with log-linear performance scaling at increased compute.

problem: Multi-modal ReID over-emphasizes low-frequency cues while overlooking mid and high-frequency structures encoding discriminative identity details.
approach: FUSE reformulates multi-modal ReID via spectral disentanglement and energy alignment, with Spectral Decomposition Module and Cross-Modal Alignment Module.
contribution: Achieves 9.1% mAP and 9.5% Rank-1 improvements on RGBNT and MSVR benchmarks with interpretable frequency-domain paradigm.

problem: Emotional text-to-speech systems enforce single utterance-level emotion, collapsing affective diversity and suppressing mixed or misaligned expression.
approach: CoCoEmo uses activation steering via latent direction vectors with quantitative controllable framework and multi-rater evaluation for composable mixed-emotion synthesis.
contribution: First systematic analysis showing emotional prosody is primarily synthesized by TTS language module, with lightweight steering for natural human-like emotional speech.

problem: Production human video generation faces challenges maintaining full-body identity consistency across dynamic shots and viewpoints without copy-paste artifacts.
approach: WildActor introduces Actor-18M dataset with 1.6M videos and 18M images covering diverse views, plus Asymmetric Identity-Preserving Attention with Viewpoint-Adaptive sampling.
contribution: Consistently preserves body identity under diverse compositions and large viewpoint transitions on Actor-Bench, surpassing existing methods.

problem: Deep RL agents trained in simulators suffer performance degradation and safety violations when deployed in real environments due to sim-to-real gap.
approach: Proposes framework using probabilistic latent embeddings to infer environment context and distributional RL with dynamically adjusted risk levels based on latent estimation accuracy.
contribution: Enables safe and efficient policy transfer via latent context inference and dynamic risk adjustment, addressing unmodeled system dynamics.

problem: Robotic agents lack principled ways to learn from mistakes, limiting their ability to diagnose failures and adapt behavior.
approach: LAGEA uses natural language feedback from vision language models as error signals, grounds feedback temporally, aligns it with visual state, and converts to adaptive shaping rewards.
contribution: Improves average success by 9.0% on random goals, 5.3% on fixed goals, and 17% on fetch tasks on Meta-World benchmarks.

problem: Flow matching planners lack formal guarantees for state/action constraint satisfaction and dynamic consistency, critical for safety and executability.
approach: SAD-Flower augments flow with virtual control enabling principled guidance from nonlinear control theory for constraint satisfaction without retraining.
contribution: Outperforms generative baselines in ensuring constraint satisfaction across tasks, enabling test-time satisfaction of unseen constraints.

problem: Dataset distillation theory lacks quantitative boundaries explaining why heterogeneous matching objectives work and when robustness breaks under configuration changes.
approach: Proposes configuration-dynamics-error analysis treating training configurations as update operators, measuring robustness via test-risk gap between distilled and full data.
contribution: Establishes two predictive laws: gap decays as O(k^-1/2) until configuration floor, and required k grows linearly with configuration diversity.

problem: Hyperspectral image change detection suffers from annotation scarcity and limited diversity when using confidence-based pseudo-label selection.
approach: IA-SFT evaluates pseudo-label influence on model decisions to identify valuable supervision, designs Adaptive Fusion Change Decoder modeling global consistency and local details.
contribution: Consistently improves pseudo-label quality and detection performance with superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Test-time compute scaling allocates computation uniformly, missing opportunities to concentrate resources on high-utility reasoning paths.
approach: Uses verifier-guided adaptive framework where process reward models guide pruning, expansion, and selection across multiple inference iterations.
contribution: Outperforms direct scaling on MATH-500 with large gains on AIME24 and AMO-Bench, concentrating computation on high-value reasoning.

problem: Existing RLVR methods treat heterogeneous-quality responses uniformly and discard rollouts after single use, leading to noisy supervision and poor efficiency.
approach: Formulates rollout scheduling as contextual bandit problem with neural scheduler adaptively selecting high-value rollouts, supporting both intra-group selection and historical reuse.
contribution: Provides theoretical regret bounds and consistent gains in performance and training efficiency across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
